trace.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.

I set up the campaign as a proposal. It goes to 56 people, not everyone who gave you a phone number, and nothing will be sent until someone approves it.

You have 2,958 customers with a phone number on file. Your policy only allows marketing texts to people who actually signed up for texts, and only 56 of them have done that and haven't unsubscribed [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. Another 1,698 just gave a number when they ordered. That lets you send them order-status texts, but not promotions. The 81 who unsubscribed can't get any texts at all.

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 10% off any pho this weekend! Offer valid through Sunday, Oct 25, 2026. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out." It follows the policy rules:

- **Discount:** 10% is under the 15% limit.
- **Offer terms:** It gives an end date within 14 days and says "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **Wording:** It names the restaurant and ends with the opt-out line [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

The automatic check passed on the discount, the wording and the 56-person list, and it doesn't need your sign-off as owner. Today is Saturday, so it should go out soon to be useful. It also has to be sent between 9am and 8pm Central [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

trace.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
trace.answer:
I didn't set up this campaign because your messaging policy forbids it. The policy says "Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. That's an outright ban, so your approval wouldn't make it allowed. The 25% discount causes a second problem: any discount over 20% in a text needs your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

Here's what the policy does allow. You could text a discount of 20% or less on items that aren't Seasonal Specials. The offer would have to expire within 7 days and could be used once per customer [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. You could also send a text about Seasonal Specials with no discount. Either way, the rules on who can get the text are the same. Customers who ordered in the last 90 days and gave a phone number can get up to two marketing texts a month. Anyone else needs verified SMS consent, and customers who unsubscribed can't be texted [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts; §4, Frequency]. Texts can't go out between 9pm and 8am Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

If you choose one of these, I can count who's eligible, write the message with opt-out wording and submit it for approval.
